Stepwise Behaviors

Stepwise Behavior enables policy-driven pipeline control at defined pipeline execution stages. Engineer-supplied Stepwise functions observe the current committed state alongside the stage-appropriate candidate value and explicitly decide whether pipeline execution should continue, block, or clear.

Stepwise Contract Summary

  • Stepwise functions must be pure and side-effect free
  • The pipeline provides Stepwise functions with isolated, read-only snapshots of both the current state and the stage-appropriate candidate value; these values must not be mutated
  • Stepwise functions do not return a value — they must emit exactly one decision: continue, block, or clear
  • Exactly one Stepwise function may be registered per supported pipeline stage
  • Errors thrown during stepwise evaluation propagate as Vault errors and terminate the current update

Stepwise behaviors participate exclusively in policy evaluation. They do not derive values, do not mutate state, and do not emit snapshots. Their sole responsibility is to determine whether a candidate value should be accepted, suppressed, or used to clear existing state.

The Stepwise contract guarantees that policy evaluation is deterministic and authoritative. If a Stepwise function throws an error, that error is promoted to a Vault error and immediately terminates the current pipeline execution. The in-flight candidate value is discarded, no decision is applied, and no snapshot is emitted. This ensures that policy failures never result in ambiguous control flow or inconsistent pipeline outcomes. For details on how referential isolation is enforced at every stage boundary, see Pipeline Isolation.

Note

Because a Stepwise behavior does not return a value, failing to invoke a decision method (continue, block, or clear) leaves the pipeline awaiting a response that never arrives. This creates a policy deadlock and prevents the FeatureCell from processing further updates.

Stepwise behaviors require the Stepwise Controller to be present. If any Stepwise behavior is configured without the Stepwise Controller, the pipeline will throw a runtime error and halt FeatureCell execution for the current update.

Stepwise Stage

The Stepwise stage executes after a pipeline stage has produced a candidate value. Depending on configuration, Stepwise evaluation may occur after the Resolve stage, the Filter stage, or the Reducer stage.

When present, the Stepwise stage executes immediately after its associated pipeline stage has produced a candidate value and before that value is admitted into downstream pipeline processing.

Stepwise functions are invoked with isolated, read-only snapshots of the current committed state and the stage-appropriate candidate value, along with a decision controller. Based on this evaluation, the function must explicitly emit exactly one execution outcome:

  • continue() — allow the candidate value to proceed through the pipeline
  • block() — suppress the candidate update while leaving existing state unchanged
  • clear() — clear the current committed state and terminate processing for this update

Stepwise functions must always emit exactly one decision. Failure to do so results in pipeline termination to preserve deterministic and safe execution semantics.

Add-on Pipeline Stage

Stepwise stages are optional, add-on behaviors within the FeatureCell lifecycle. The Stepwise Controller and individual Stepwise behaviors are registered as part of the FeatureCell’s declarative configuration. Individual Stepwise behaviors are attached exclusively through the fluent API during FeatureCell initialization, ensuring that stage control is defined explicitly at startup rather than embedded into static configuration.

Fluent Stepwise APIs

A FeatureCell may declare Stepwise behavior for supported pipeline stages using the .withStepwiseResolve(), .withStepwiseFilter(), and .withStepwiseReducer() fluent APIs. Each API accepts a single Stepwise callback function for its respective stage.

Stepwise behaviors execute in the Processing Layer at their associated pipeline stage. The order in which Stepwise APIs are declared does not affect pipeline execution order.

Providing a Stepwise configuration without a valid callback function results in a Vault error and prevents pipeline execution.

Note

Although multiple Stepwise stages may be configured across the pipeline, each should have a clearly defined and isolated policy responsibility. Because Stepwise behaviors directly influence pipeline admission and state control, combining complex or overlapping policies can introduce interactions that are difficult to reason about or debug.

Diagrams
Available Stepwise Behaviors

Stepwise behaviors are optional, engineer-selected policy behaviors attached during FeatureCell initialization. They may be sourced from /addons or implemented directly by engineers to enforce feature-specific or domain-specific policy constraints.

Regardless of origin, all Stepwise behaviors execute exclusively within the Processing Layer and must respect stage responsibility boundaries. Stepwise behaviors influence whether a candidate update is admitted into the pipeline, without deriving values, mutating state, or participating in computation.

Pre-built Stepwise Controller
Addon Controller Description Package
withStepwiseController

type: controller

 Coordinates Stepwise policy evaluation by mediating decision requests and responses between Stepwise behaviors and the pipeline. The controller is required whenever any Stepwise behavior is configured. /addons
Pre-built Stepwise Behaviors
Addon Behavior Description Package
withStepwiseFilterBehavior

stage: Stepwise Filter

type: policy

 Executes an engineer-supplied Stepwise Filter function immediately after the Filter stage produces a filtered candidate value. The function evaluates pipeline state and emits a control decision that determines whether execution continues, is suppressed, or clears existing state.
  • Does not mutate state
  • Does not derive or return values
  • Maps decisions to Vault-native control signals
 /addons
withStepwiseReducerBehavior

stage: Stepwise Reducer

type: policy

 Executes an engineer-supplied Stepwise Reducer function immediately after the Reducer stage produces a reduced candidate value. The function evaluates pipeline state and emits a control decision that determines whether execution continues, is suppressed, or clears existing state.
  • Does not mutate state
  • Does not derive or return values
  • Maps decisions to Vault-native control signals
 /addons
withStepwiseResolveBehavior

stage: Stepwise Resolve

type: policy

 Executes an engineer-supplied Stepwise Resolve function immediately after the Resolve stage produces a resolved candidate value. The function evaluates pipeline state and emits a control decision that determines whether execution continues, is suppressed, or clears existing state.
  • Does not mutate state
  • Does not derive or return values
  • Maps decisions to Vault-native control signals
 /addons
StepwiseStageTypes
Stage Description
filter Indicates that the Stepwise behavior executes immediately after the Filter stage has produced a filtered candidate value.
reducer Indicates that the Stepwise behavior executes immediately after the Reducer stage has produced a reduced candidate value.
resolve Indicates that the Stepwise behavior executes immediately after the Resolve stage has produced a resolved candidate value.
Examples

Stepwise behaviors are enabled by registering the Stepwise Controller and one or more Stepwise behaviors during FeatureCell initialization.

Example 1: Configuring a FeatureCell with Stepwise behaviors

In this example, Stepwise Filter, Stepwise Reducer, and Stepwise Resolve behaviors are all attached. Each behavior executes at its corresponding pipeline stage regardless of the order in which the fluent APIs are declared. Execution order is determined exclusively by pipeline stage, not by fluent configuration order. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [] 
      },
      [
        // Stepwise behaviors are registered declaratively
        withStepwiseFilterBehavior,
        withStepwiseReducerBehavior,
        withStepwiseResolveBehavior,
      ],
      [
        // Stepwise Controller is required
        withStepwiseController
      ]
    );
  ]
}

// Attach Stepwise callbacks during initialization
@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply one or more operators during initialization
    this.vault
      .withStepwiseFilter({
        stepwiseCallback: fn()
      })
      .withStepwiseReducer({
        stepwiseCallback: fn()
      })
      .withStepwiseResolve({
        stepwiseCallback: fn()
      })
    .initialize();
    
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Stepwise behaviors are registered declaratively
    withStepwiseFilterBehavior,
    withStepwiseReducerBehavior,
    withStepwiseResolveBehavior,
  ],
  [
    // Stepwise Controller is required
    withStepwiseController
  ]
);

// Attach Stepwise callbacks during initialization
employeeCell
  .withStepwiseFilter({
    stepwiseCallback: fn()
  })
  .withStepwiseReducer({
    stepwiseCallback: fn()
  })
  .withStepwiseResolve({
    stepwiseCallback: fn()
  })
  .initialize();`}}
